subject: Re: Change request — SKU provisioning & SOW adjustments (requested add-on capacity)
messages:
From: Jordan Shepard <j.shepard@acmeai.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmeai.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Change request — add reserved SKUs and adjust implementation window

Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to accelerate the private deployment and add a small reserved SKU pool up front while keeping the remainder on burst. Attached is the OrderForm SKU map (ACME_OrderForm_SKU_map.xlsx) showing: 10 reserved vGPU SKUs for 12 months + a projected burst buffer. We need the change documented as a Change Order on top of the existing MSA.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a one-time proration for the month of provisioning (we'd expect a 50% charge for the partial month)?
- Can you confirm the implementation window (requested start: 2026-10-27, target live: 2026-11-09)?

I’ve cc'd our legal team for redlines. If this looks straightforward we can agree to a short mutual action plan and route to DocuSign.

Regards,
Jordan Shepard
Head of Platform Ops, Acme AI
attachments: ACME_OrderForm_SKU_map.xlsx

---

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Jordan Shepard <j.shepard@acmeai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Change request — add reserved SKUs and adjust implementation window

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SKU map. High level: we can accommodate the 10 reserved vGPU SKUs and the proposed provisioning window. I’ve looped in Neha (legal) and Laura (procurement) to run the redlines and confirm billing/proration.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Legal redline: Neha to send back an MSA + Change Order redline (I asked for explicit language on billing proration and SLA applicability to reserved SKUs).
2) Procurement: Laura to confirm whether the order can be invoiced on the 1st of the month with a proration credit, or if we need to invoice pro rata from start date.
3) Implementation: Engineering will queue provisioning for the 10 SKUs on 2026-10-27 pending countersignature; target live 2026-11-09 as requested.

We will prepare a short amendment (Change Order) and a mutual action plan (MAP) for signature. For transparency, I attached a preliminary MSA_redline_v3.pdf with a few operative edits (billing and Annex B references).

Can you confirm the billing contact and the person who will sign on behalf of Acme? Once I have that we’ll put the DocuSign envelope together.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_redline_v3.pdf

---

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Jordan Shepard <j.shepard@acmeai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Change request — legal redlines and short summary

Team / Jordan —

I reviewed the MSA and the attached OrderForm SKU map. Below are the principal redline items and suggested language for the Change Order:

1) Billing proration: Redwood agrees to a one-time proration credit equal to 50% of the first month’s reserved SKU fees if the provisioning happens after the 15th of the month. Proposed clause: "For initial provisioning periods commencing after the fifteenth (15th) day of a calendar month, Redwood will apply a one-time proration credit equal to fifty percent (50%) of the monthly reserved SKU charges for said month."

2) SLA and reserved SKUs: Reserved SKUs will be covered under the existing SLA (Annex B). We will add language clarifying that latency/availability SLOs apply to reserved capacity first, burst capacity is best-effort.

3) Termination & rollback: Add a short rollback process if provisioning impacts production (30-day remediation window + opt-out for Acme).

4) Data residency & audit: Confirm same residency obligations as MSA; Redwood to provide audit logs for provisioned SKUs upon request (sample format: CSV with timestamps).

5) Signatures & timeline: Request Acme countersign by 2026-10-20 to meet provisioning date. If Acme needs an extended timeline, we will provide a new MAP and updated implementation dates.

I’m attaching markups as a PDF. Laura — can you confirm invoice timing? If procurement prefers monthly invoicing on the 1st we will need to coordinate proration mechanics with Finance.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_redline_v3.pdf

---

From: Jordan Shepard <j.shepard@acmeai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmeai.com
Date: 2026-10-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Change request — legal redlines and short summary

Neha, Mateo —

Appreciate the quick review. Two quick replies from Acme legal/procurement:

- The 50% proration is acceptable, though our finance team asks that the credit be applied on the invoice rather than as a retrospective credit line item (i.e., invoice net amount should reflect the proration).
- We’d like the rollback clause tightened: rather than a 30-day remediation, can we add a 10-business-day remediation period for initial provisioning incidents and an automatic pause to burst traffic if SLA thresholds are not met?

On signatures: I will be the signatory for commercial terms; I’ve copied procurement@acmeai.com in case they need to route internally. We aim to countersign by 2026-10-18. Please put the DocuSign envelope to me (j.shepard@acmeai.com).

Also, two small asks from our engineering team: can you share an implementation Gantt and the expected roll-back steps in bullet form? If you already have one, please attach — that will help our internal change advisory board.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Platform Ops, Acme AI
attachments: none
